text: Can I go back and prevent you from explaining that to me?

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Same paradox. If you were to travel back in time and, say, knock me unconscious, you would not then have the conversation that irritated you, motivating you to go back and knock me unconscious.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: What if I knocked you unconscious right now?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: But it would make the present so much nicer.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Well, it was a number of things. First the late hour, then your demeanour seems very low energy, plus your irritability... Oh! I don't usually pick up on those things. Good for me.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Oh, wait. Did you want to talk about what's bothering you?

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Wow, I' m on fire tonight.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Uh, here's the thing. Girls like Penny never end up with guys who own time machines.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I disagree. Your inability to successfully woo Penny long predates your acquisition of the time machine. That failure clearly stands on its own.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: In addition, your premise is flawed. In the original film, Rod Taylor got Yvette Mimeaux with that very time machine. In Back to the Future, Marty McFly got the opportunity to hook up with his extremely attractive young mother.
